description: Log a film the user watched to their Movie Diary (the movies page, with its poster), not log_event or log_moment. title (+ year when known), watched_at YYYY-MM-DD or a local time, rating 0-10 only if they gave one, rewatch, where, with (their contacts only), notes. The same film on the same day returns the stored watch (duplicate: true); a rewatch on another day is a new watch. Private by default. Also adds the private 'Watched:' calendar entry the diary keeps. ($0.10; API key required)

rating.description: Their score out of 10, only if given.

request_id.description: Client idempotency key (retries return original result).

watched_at.description: Local YYYY-MM-DD (last night = yesterday), or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM if they gave a time. Omit for now.

watched_at_precision.description: approximate when a part of day was read as a time.

with.description: Who with; only their contacts are kept.

name: log_movie_watch

account.description: The Dayze account this data belongs to. With more than one Dayze connection, name it in the answer.

note.description: How to disclose the account to the user.

qa_fixture.description: True for a known QA test account: its records are fixture data, not a real life.

duplicate.description: True when the same film was already logged that day; nothing was added.

inspect_note.description: What inspect_url opens. Never quote the record id.

inspect_url.description: The Dayze page that shows the saved record.

provenance.description: Which connector wrote the record and which connected Dayze account received it.

note.description: How to disclose the account to the user.

name.description: The connected app or API-key label shown to the account owner.

source.description: chatgpt for ChatGPT OAuth writes; mcp for another OAuth app or API key.

watch.description: The diary entry: watch_id, title, year, watched_on, rating, rewatch, poster_url, visibility.
